relations.subject: server:rebalance
relations.evidence: This indicates that hard failover has successfully completed, but a rebalance is required to complete the reduction of the two-node cluster to one node.

relations.subject: server:hard-failover
relations.evidence: Performing a hard failover on a node containing vBuckets that have no replicas on other nodes results in data loss.

relations.subject: server:unsafe-hard-failover
relations.evidence: If hard failover must nevertheless be performed, the `failover` CLI expression should be re-entered: this time, with the `--force` flag used, in addition to the `--hard` flag. This produces an _unsafe_ hard failover.

relations.subject: server:hard-failover
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate; a judgment call capturing that normal (safe-mode) hard failover refuses in certain circumstances and only the unsafe variant proceeds
relations.evidence: In certain circumstances, an attempted hard failover will not be executed by Couchbase Server: for information, see [Hard Failover in Default and Unsafe Modes](../../learn/clusters-and-availability/hard-failover.md#default-and-unsafe). Such an attempt therefore fails, with an `ERROR: Received unexpected status 504` notification.

relations.subject: server:node-recovery
relations.evidence: A node that has been failed over can be recovered and reintegrated into the cluster. See [Recover a Node](recover-nodes.md).

relations.subject: server:hard-failover
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate; a judgment call, object stands in for the auto-failover retry-quota counter reset by a manual rebalance
relations.evidence: Note that a rebalance, which can be started by left-clicking on the **Rebalance** button, also resets this count to zero, on successful completion.

relations.subject: server:hard-failover
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate; a judgment call standing in for 'the total number of nodes failed over exceeding a bucket's replica count', since the registry has no dedicated concept for that multi-node data-loss threshold
relations.evidence: For hard failover of multiple nodes, each Couchbase bucket must have at least as many replicas as the total number of nodes failed over or you WILL lose data.

notable_absence.finding: No role requirement is stated for hard failover either, matching the pattern across every failover-family page in this batch. Also notable: the CLI and REST surfaces disagree on the ERROR SIGNAL for a refused hard failover - the CLI page states 'ERROR: Received unexpected status 504' while the REST section of this SAME page states 'Cannot safely perform a failover at the moment' for what appears to be the identical refused-failover condition. Flagged as a possible docs-issue (inconsistent error reporting across two surfaces of the same operation on one page) rather than modeled as two different conditions, since nothing on the page states they differ.

cross_component_finding: Hard failover surfaces a real structural fork the round's hypothesis anticipated: a SAFE mode (default, refuses under risk) and an UNSAFE mode (explicit override, proceeds anyway) are not just a flag on the same call - the unsafe path is reached only after the safe path has already failed, is invoked with materially different parameters (--force/--hard vs. allowUnsafe=true on the rebalance call itself, not on failover), and multiple-node hard failover has its own dedicated UI surface (the FAILOVER tab) not shared with single-node hard failover's row-level button. 'Hard failover' is therefore itself closer to a small family (single-node / multiple-node / unsafe) than one uniform operation, mirroring this round's central question about rebalance but one level up the call stack.
